title: Fraction walls and families
li: We are learning to build a fraction wall and sort fractions into families.
sc: I can build a fraction wall with halves, quarters, eighths and thirds
I can explain that a fraction family has the same denominator
I can use the wall to see which parts are longer or shorter
materials: paper strips all the same length

slides.title: Warm-up: Mixed review
items: 1/3 of a rope is 4 m. How long is the whole rope?
Which is longer: 1/2 or 1/8 of the same strip?

slides.title: Building a fraction wall

rows.label: Same whole
rows.text: Every row is the same length. Each row is one whole.

rows.label: Halving
rows.text: Halve each part to get the next row: 2, then 4, then 8 parts.

rows.label: Line up
rows.text: Look down the wall. 1/2 lines up with 2/4 and 4/8.

slides.notes: Build the wall in front of the class with strips you folded in earlier lessons. Ask students to predict where each fold will be before you open it.

slides.title: Thirds and sixths

rows.label: Thirds
rows.text: Made by estimate and adjust, not by halving.

rows.label: Sixths
rows.text: Halve each third to make sixths. 1/3 lines up with 2/6.

slides.notes: Ask: does 1/2 line up with anything on the thirds row? (No. It lines up with 3/6.)

slides.means: Fractions with the same denominator. The whole is cut into the same number of equal parts.
slides.example: 1/8, 3/8, 5/8 and 8/8 all belong to the eighths family.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.text: Look only at the denominator. It names the family.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.text: In one family the parts are the same size, so more parts is further along: 1/4 < 3/4.

slides.title: Turn and talk
slides.prompt: Ruby says 3/4 and 3/8 are in the same family because they both have a 3. Do you agree? Explain.
slides.notes: Disagree. The family is named by the denominator. 3/4 is in the quarters family and 3/8 is in the eighths family.

slides.title: Which one?
slides.question: Which set is one fraction family?
why: Wrong: this child grouped by the top number. The denominators are all different.
Right: all have denominator 5, so they belong to the fifths family.
Wrong: these land on the same point, but they are in different families.
Wrong: these follow a counting pattern, but every denominator is different.

slides.title: Show me: families
questions: Write the thirds family from 1/3 to one whole.
Which quarters fraction lines up with 1/2?
How many sixths line up with 1/3?

slides.title: Activity: Wall and match
steps: Fold and cut strips to build your own wall: whole, halves, quarters, eighths and thirds.
Glue the rows. Label every part and colour each family.
Play Fraction Match with a partner.
Then do your level on the Fraction families sheet.
slides.notes: All strips must be the same length or the wall will not line up. Pre-cut strips save time.

slides.support: Use the fraction wall to colour each family and label the parts. Name the family of each fraction.
slides.core: Sort fractions into families, order one family, and use the wall to find parts that line up.
slides.extend: Find fractions on the wall that line up with 2/3 and 3/4. Why does 1/2 have no match in thirds?

questions: What does every fraction in one family share?
What did the wall show you about the size of the parts?
slides.connect: We built a fraction wall and sorted fractions into families. Which success criteria can you tick?
slides.notes: Add the Fraction families panel to the flip book.

teach.text: A family has the same denominator. 1/4, 2/4, 3/4 and 4/4 are the quarters family.

items.q: Circle the fractions in the thirds family: 1/3, 3/4, 2/3, 3/8
Use the wall. Which is longer: 1/4 or 1/8?

teach.text: In one family the parts are the same size, so compare the numerators: 2/8 is less than 5/8.

items.q: Order the eighths from smallest to largest: 5/8, 1/8, 8/8, 3/8
Use the wall. Which fractions line up with 1/2?
Ruby says 3/4 and 3/8 are in the same family. Is she right? Explain.
items.answer: No. They have different denominators, so they are in different families (quarters and eighths).

items.q: What fraction is marked? Name its family.

teach.text: Halving makes new families: halves to quarters to eighths, and thirds to sixths.

items.q: Which sixths fraction lines up with 2/3?
Which eighths fraction lines up with 3/4?
1/2 has no exact match in the thirds family. Explain why.
items.answer: Halfway falls in the middle of the second third, so it is not on a thirds mark. 3 thirds cannot be shared into 2 equal groups of whole thirds.

items.q: Order these unit fractions from smallest to largest: 1/3, 1/8, 1/2, 1/4
Write 2 fractions from different families that both land on 1.

printables.title: Fraction Match cards
printables.instructions: Cut out and shuffle. Lay face down. Flip 2 cards. Keep them if the fraction matches the picture. Bonus point: name the family.

teacherNotes: The syllabus asks students to see that fractions made from the same number of equal parts form a family with the same denominator. The wall is the main model today, so make sure every row starts and ends at the same place. Some students will group by numerator; the hinge question finds them quickly. Lining up fractions such as 1/2 and 2/4 is a preview of equivalence, so treat it as noticing rather than a skill to master.

exitTicket.q: Which two are in the same family: 2/3, 2/5, 1/3?
